goal: Improve the lint script for subtree updates to check that new subtree merges are stacked on the previous subtree merge
This makes it possible to reuse the exact same merge commit hash when backporting subtree fixes to multiple release branches, saving reviewers from re-reviewing
reviewability: Ready, two contributors have code-reviewed and tested the latest commit
agreement: Strong support: ryanofsky and BrandonOdiwuor both gave code review ACKs on the final commit after testing the behavior (ryanofsky, BrandonOdiwuor)
Early skepticism about whether this solves a real problem was answered with concrete evidence of past backports using the technique (sedited, maflcko, Sjors)
ryanofsky's earlier concerns about vague docs and confusing warning text were addressed by revising the script and docs (ryanofsky)

result.summary: This PR updates test/lint/git-subtree-check.sh to verify that the most recent subtree merge is based on (stacked on) the previous subtree merge commit, rather than a later commit on master, erroring if not. An --incompatible flag is added to explicitly bypass this check when subtree and Bitcoin Core code are incompatible. It also refactors the script's option parsing from getopts to explicit parsing and adds documentation in developer-notes.md and test/lint/README.md.
result.problem: Subtree updates that aren't stacked on the previous subtree merge require reviewers to re-review a freshly generated merge commit when backporting to release branches, instead of reusing an already-reviewed commit hash. This wastes reviewer time on every backport of a subtree fix.

resolved_concerns: sedited questioned whether this solves a real problem; Sjors showed prior backports (#34804, #34952) that reused identical merge hashes thanks to this practice
maflcko asked how this helps and raised the case where a build fix must live in the merge commit itself; addressed via --incompatible flag and discussion

ryanofsky's initial review flagged vague docs, confusing warning text, and a partial-check gap; Sjors force-pushed a revision addressing all three points, and ryanofsky then gave a full code review ACK
ryanofsky suggested optionally documenting how to check out the previous merge base; Sjors decided to leave the docs as-is for now, and ryanofsky did not push back further

result.card: This PR extends test/lint/git-subtree-check.sh to verify that a new subtree merge is stacked on the previous subtree merge, adding an --incompatible escape hatch when that isn't possible, plus documentation updates. The problem is that non-stacked subtree merges force reviewers to re-review a freshly generated merge commit for every release-branch backport instead of reusing an already-reviewed commit hash; Sjors cites #34804 and #34952 as real examples where this saved reviewer effort. Both ryanofsky and BrandonOdiwuor gave code-review ACKs on the final commit after testing the behavior, and earlier skepticism from sedited and maflcko was resolved with concrete evidence. The PR is Ready for merge with no open concerns. It belongs to both the tests (lint framework) and docs categories, ranking P3 in each since the benefit is real but narrow to the infrequent subtree-update workflow.
